stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a vital event?

explanation.en: Vital events are births, deaths, marriages, divorces and migration. Admission to a college is not a vital event.

stem.en: In India the population census is conducted once in every

explanation.en: The Indian census is decennial: it is taken once in ten years (1951, 1961, …, 2011).

stem.en: The population of a town was 2,40,000 on 1 January and 2,60,000 on 31 December. There were 6,000 live births in the year. Taking the mean of the two counts as the mid-year population, the crude birth rate is
Vital rates are usually expressed

options.en: as a ratio of males to females

explanation.en: Vital rates such as birth and death rates are expressed per 1000 of the (mid-year) population.

stem.en: In the registration method of collecting vital statistics, the events are recorded

options.en: continuously, as and when they occur
only for a sample of villages once
only at the time of a general election

explanation.en: Registration is a continuous process: births and deaths are registered with the local registrar as they happen (Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969).

stem.en: The crude death rate (CDR) of a population is

explanation.en: CDR = (total deaths in the year / mid-year population) × 1000.

stem.en: In a town with population 50,000, there were 600 deaths in a year. The CDR is

explanation.en: CDR = 600/50,000 × 1000 = 12 per thousand.

stem.en: The main drawback of the crude death rate is that it

options.en: cannot be calculated from census data
ignores the age and sex composition of the population

explanation.en: CDR treats every person alike, so two towns with different age structures cannot be fairly compared by CDR.

stem.en: In the age group 50+ a town has 4,000 persons and 200 deaths. Its specific death rate for this group is

explanation.en: SDR = 200/4,000 × 1000 = 50 per thousand.

stem.en: The crude death rate equals the weighted arithmetic mean of the specific death rates, the weights being

options.en: the populations of the age groups
the deaths in the age groups

explanation.en: CDR = Σ(Pₓ·SDRₓ)/ΣPₓ because Pₓ·SDRₓ/1000 = Dₓ, the deaths of each group.

stem.en: The standardised death rate (direct method) of a town is

options.en: Σ(Aₓ · SDRₓ) / ΣAₓ, where Aₓ is the standard population

explanation.en: Apply the town's own SDRs to a common standard population and take the weighted mean.

stem.en: Standardised death rates are preferred to crude death rates for comparing two towns because they

options.en: remove the effect of different age compositions

explanation.en: Both towns are referred to the same standard population, so only the age-wise death rates make the difference.

stem.en: Standard population: 3,000, 5,000, 2,000 in age groups 0–15, 15–50, 50+. Town A has SDRs 12, 5, 40. The STDR of A is
Town A has CDR 13.4 and STDR 14.1; town B has CDR 11.5 and STDR 15.0. Which statement is correct?

options.en: A is healthier, because its STDR is lower
B is healthier, because its CDR is lower

explanation.en: Healthiness is compared on standardised rates, which remove the age-structure effect. A has the lower STDR.

stem.en: The general fertility rate (GFR) is

explanation.en: GFR relates births to women in the child-bearing age group 15–49 only.

stem.en: A town has 7,200 women aged 15–49 and 576 live births in a year. The GFR is

explanation.en: GFR = 576/7,200 × 1000 = 80 per thousand women of child-bearing age.

stem.en: The specific fertility rates (per thousand) of the seven 5-year age groups 15–19, …, 45–49 add up to 565. The total fertility rate is

explanation.en: TFR = i × ΣSFR = 5 × 565 = 2,825 per thousand women (about 2.825 children per woman).

stem.en: Which fertility rate gives the number of children a woman would bear in her child-bearing life at current age-specific rates?

explanation.en: TFR adds the age-specific rates over the whole child-bearing span (15–49).

stem.en: The gross reproduction rate (GRR) is calculated using

explanation.en: Reproduction rates measure how women replace themselves, so only female births are counted.

stem.en: If the net reproduction rate (NRR) of a population is less than 1, the population will

explanation.en: NRR < 1: each woman is replaced by fewer than one daughter who survives, so the population tends to decline.

stem.en: For any population, the correct order is

explanation.en: GRR counts only daughters (a part of TFR) and NRR further multiplies by survival ratios (≤ 1).

stem.en: The female specific fertility rates (per thousand women) for 15–19, …, 45–49 are 15, 72, 88, 58, 29, 10, 2. The GRR per woman is

explanation.en: GRR = 5 × ΣFSFR = 5 × 274 = 1,370 per thousand women = 1.37 per woman.

stem.en: In a life table, dₓ is

explanation.en: dₓ is the number dying between age x and x + 1: those alive at x minus those alive at x + 1.

stem.en: The complete expectation of life at age x is

explanation.en: Tₓ is the total years to be lived after age x by the lₓ persons alive at x, so the average is Tₓ/lₓ.

Assuming deaths are spread evenly over the year, Lₓ in a life table is

explanation.en: Lₓ is the number of years lived between x and x + 1; with uniform deaths it is the mean of lₓ and lₓ₊₁.

stem.en: Life tables are used by life insurance companies mainly to

explanation.en: Premiums depend on the probabilities of survival and death at each age, which the life table gives.

stem.en: With the female specific fertility rates 15, 72, 88, 58, 29, 10, 2 (per thousand, 5-year groups 15–49) and survival ratios 0.95, 0.94, 0.93, 0.92, 0.9, 0.88, 0.85, the NRR per woman is

explanation.en: NRR = 5 × Σ(FSFR × S) = 5 × 253.73 = 1268.65 per thousand = 1.269 per woman. It is above 1, so the population is growing.

stem.en: In a life table for 1000 laboratory rats, T₂ = 2,280 and l₂ = 860. The expectation of life at age 2 is

explanation.en: e₂⁰ = T₂/l₂ = 2,280/860 = 2.65 years (further years of life after age 2).
